This slice defines private receipt-bearing visual-action helpers using only standard-library orchestration, as stated in the module docstring and imports through line 28.
Provider-key shapes are anchored at a token boundary and length-bounded, plus a PEM private-key header branch. Each branch names its body for evidence checking.
_key_body judges only the body after the prefix: needs 8+ distinct chars, plus case and digit rules that differ for generic, Slack, and other kinds.
is_secret is the credential gate: true only for credential-shaped tokens or PEM headers, false for non-string, empty, or non-matching input.
run bounds both time and collected output, kills the process group on failure, and fails with command time budget exceeded, subprocess output budget exceeded, or command failed.
Frame storage requires tmpfs validation; otherwise it fails with frames require tmpfs.
In plain words: screenshots or frame writes just fail with a frames error when the RAM-disk check does not pass, even if disk space looks fine.
RAM-root setup refuses symlinks and wrong ownership, failing with symlink in RAM root or RAM root owned by another uid, so later job dirs stay owned and unlinked.
jobpath accepts only names matching a restricted pattern and refuses symlink jobs, failing with invalid job or symlink job refused.
state_lock serializes job-state access with an exclusive file lock on a per-job lock file.
save_unlocked assigns a run id if missing and atomically publishes canonical JSON by writing a temp file then renaming over job.json.
Recorded PIDs are compared in-namespace only; records made before the field existed are treated as host-namespace records.
budget walks the job tree excluding private caches and symlinks and fails with job RAM budget exceeded when total exceeds 2 GiB.

select_refs starts from defaults, then optionally pins refs from a dependency lock object, failing with symlink dependency lock refused, dependency lock too large, invalid dependency lock, or duplicate dependency entry.
engines() turns pinned wender and ve commits from select_refs into ready-to-use cached directories, creating one locked per-SHA entry via git archive with member validation and read-only permissions.

capture(j) is the screenshot entry: it prunes and budgets, verifies target liveness, then captures by web RPC, by framebuffer helper, or by x11grab, and budgets again before returning the new frame path.
desktop_env() builds on engine_env(), ensures per-job home and config dirs exist, sets DISPLAY plus locale and portal flags, and strips session bus and auth variables to isolate the desktop session.

lifecycle() serializes job operations on a job lock file; without wait it fails fast with job operation in progress, with wait it polls until a bounded limit then fails with budget exceeded, and it refuses a symlink lock.
actor() allows one actor per display using a stable lock file outside any job dir derived from the display identity; it is non-blocking and fails with another actor holds this display.
display_identity() normalizes local screens on the same X server to a shared key so colon N and colon N dot M exclude each other, while non-local display strings pass through unchanged.

Pin and cache validation fails with invalid commit pin, engine pin is not a full commit SHA, symlink engine cache refused, unsafe engine archive, and engine commit unavailable, stopping engine setup before use.
target() fails with scope memory budget exceeded, recorded target process died, owned target process is stopped, target window absent or unresponsive, and window owner stopped or dead.
oom_count() reads the cgroup event counter and oom_killed() compares it to the stored base; test jobs record a base at start so only kills after start count as scope exhaustion.

In plain words: the window is still visible but the app does not react. responsive() returns False when the optional loop probe exits 7, while timeouts and other target failures still propagate and pixel checks stay in force.

desktop_responsive() depends on window search and property tools plus in-target probes: Tk send on authorized targets and ping round-trip, failing with Tk target event loop did not respond or target did not answer ping.

Engine materialization extracts an untrusted archive into a temp dir, rejects absolute or dot-dot members and non-regular entries, hardens file permissions, then atomically renames and cleans the temp dir on failure.

Engine source directories are overridable by environment variables per engine, while pins default when no target repo is set or when the lock is absent; selection reasons record why each default or pinned value was chosen.

rpc() sends one JSON line over the job helper socket with short timeout for ping and longer timeout otherwise, fails with target helper unavailable on transport errors, and re-raises remote errors with their code.
_decode_png is an independent PNG decoder for 8-bit RGB/RGBA captures, not an engine assertion; pixels() caches decoded RGB frames content-addressed by file hash for reuse.
A capture PNG must have depth 8, color type 2 or 3-channel/4-channel, no interlace, and w*h<=16777216; decoded length must equal (stride+1)*h or it is rejected.
PNG decode fails with exact strings: 'invalid capture PNG', 'capture PNG CRC failed', 'unsupported capture PNG', 'capture PNG lacks header', 'capture PNG length mismatch', 'unsupported PNG filter'.

pixel_evidence decodes before/after (or reuses supplied pixels), fails if sizes differ with 'capture dimensions changed', overwrites masked rectangles with before bytes, then reports different/in_region plus sha_before/sha_after.

describe(frame,prev,masks) runs vadapt.cu_describe with --frame --marks-out --ocr-marks --json, validates dict with list marks and changed_regions else 'invalid vision-engine observation', then records frame paths and frame_sha256.
prune_frames keeps at most 40-reserve frame_*.png files, deletes paired marks and crops, counts frames_dropped and oldest_retained_step, then saves.
redact replaces each credential-shaped substring verified by is_secret with [redacted] and truncates the result to 200 chars for receipts.

receipt builds schema vis.receipt/v1 with job, run_id, step, verb, action, verdict pass if rc 0 else refused for rc 2,4,5 else fail, redacts reason, hashes actions longer than 80 chars or secret-shaped, and appends to receipts file.
rect requires string X,Y,W,H with non-negative X,Y and positive W,H else 'rectangle requires X,Y,W,H'; intersects tests axis-aligned overlap.

read_type_file only opens a regular non-symlink file inside the job RAM dir, at most 64 KB, UTF-8, using lstat plus O_NOFOLLOW open and dev/ino recheck; refusals use 'type-file must be inside the job RAM dir; not opened', 'type-file must be a regular non-symlink file; not opened', 'type-file larger than 64 KB', 'type-file is not UTF-8', 'type-file changed while opening'.
rule refuses with 'attached display is read-only', 'credential-shaped token refused; vis never types real secrets', 'AX is web only', 'unknown AX node', 'protected input refused'.

visible_node requires 4-element box else 'target visible geometry unavailable' and positive size plus not hidden; state_observation requires wender.state/v1 dict with node list else 'STATE unavailable or malformed', matching counts without truncated/incomplete else 'STATE incomplete', and RootWebArea else 'STATE root absent'.

do_act defaults missing expect_change to any, rejects inherited display with 'inherited display is not owned', then serializes one job act with a blocking lifecycle lock and non-blocking display-wide actor exclusion.

do_act setup fails with '--expect-change exit needs a started desktop or electron job', 'settle budget invalid', 'AX requires --op', 'AX type requires --text', 'step already passed', 'step retry budget spent'.
In plain words: I try to click a number from look and it says marks are stale or the mark is gone, so I have to run look again to get fresh marks before clicking.

Tail of do_act performs the input between before/after captures then verifies it: web RPC action versus xdotool click/type/key, with a dedicated exit-wait branch versus a timed pixel-settle sampling branch that ends in a receipt.
serve(name) is the long-lived supervisor entry: sets subreaper, loads job.json, launches Xvfb and web/desktop targets, records cgroup and pids, binds helper.sock and signals ready for helper ops.

After-frames flow from capture through cached pixels decode into pixel_evidence with masks and region, tracking transient/onset/stable digests, then describe output is filtered by actual_change before receipt and saved state.

Exit expectation has its own terminal state: on success it stores before, no after, clears changed_regions and marks_valid False, writes exit receipt and returns; on failure it writes reason receipt then raises.

Pass for sampled acts requires verified plus: any needs non-empty regions and different pixels; none needs no regions, no transient and no different; rectangle needs in_region and intersection with a reported region.

Exit-wait failures include exact strings 'scope memory budget exceeded' on OOM, 'client exited 0 but another owned process exited: ' plus details, and 'expected exit not observed; target still running' on settle timeout.
Sampled-act mismatch fails rc 3 with exact reason 'expected visible change not verified' in both the receipt reason field and the raised Failure.
In plain words: I clicked or typed and nothing seemed to change, then the tool reported expected visible change not verified; or it said the mark is stale and I must run look again before clicking.

Supervisor serializes helper.sock requests in one accept loop handling stop, ping, capture, state, protected and action; once a child exit sets dead True it writes target.exit.json and every later op fails from that witness.

Xvfb is started with a displayfd pipe and 10 s deadline; the supervisor reads until newline, rejects empty read as 'incomplete Xvfb displayfd response', long garbage as 'invalid Xvfb displayfd response', and non-digits the same.
Web capture path is constrained: parent must equal the job root and must not be a symlink, otherwise fail 5 with exact string 'capture path refused' before capturing screenshot bytes.
Desktop actuation depends on xdotool: mousemove --sync plus mousedown/mouseup for xy, type --clearmodifiers -- for type text, and key --clearmodifiers -- for key input.
Web target keeps all browser profile data inside the job by overriding TMPDIR to the job root and selects headless versus headed Chrome with device metrics override from the job size.
The helper loop inside serve executes web pointer and text actions: pointer move plus press and release with short sleeps marked verified, and direct text insertion marked verified.
Web action without pointer coordinates, text, or AX target fails with rc 7 and reason 'web key input unavailable'; handler exceptions become rc 8 or the Failure rc with the exception message.

Serve shutdown in finally ignores termination signals, closes the automation channel and socket, then reaps owned descendants with graceful terminate plus continue, short wait, kill, then non-blocking waitpid until no child remains.

scope_members returns no members when scope or cgroup record is missing or the scope directory is gone or membership data vanishes; otherwise it verifies scope name shape, resolved location, and manager-reported ownership before reading integer member PIDs.
Scope validation fails closed with rc 5 'scope identity invalid', 'scope path invalid', or 'scope ownership not verified' when name, location, or manager ownership checks disagree.

shutdown_started collects live records plus owned descendants and scope members into cleanup_pids, saves, asks the helper to stop, then waits and escalates from terminate to kill before declaring failure.
Shutdown fails with rc 8 'owned process did not stop or reap; job retained' if any record remains present, and 'owned scope is not empty; job retained' if scope members remain.
Test isolation uses a small subreaper wrapper that reports the supervisor PID then reaps orphans, enabled only when the test flag is set inside a non-initial PID namespace.
Test-mode start requires the caller cgroup to carry a numeric memory limit; otherwise it fails rc 5 with 'test-mode start needs a memory-capped caller cgroup (safe_run)'.

launch_test_supervisor starts the serve command with a minimal preserved environment, logs to scope output, and reads a numeric PID line within the remaining budget; non-numeric output fails rc 7 'test-mode supervisor launch failed'.

Production start needs a usable user session runtime: an owned absolute runtime directory, scheduler executables, and a reachable user manager; the probe returns missing prerequisites without side effects.
Missing session runtime raises rc 7 with reason prefixed 'session_runtime_absent: ' and details cause 'session_runtime_absent' plus the joined prerequisite list.

start validates size shape, timeout range, memory cap shape, absence of an existing job, and engine pins before creating the job directory; violations fail rc 2 'invalid size', 'timeout out of range', 'invalid memory cap', or 'job already exists'.

start creates a started job record with display, target kind, size, engines, owner, scope identity, and namespace, then launches either the test supervisor or a nested user scope plus service and waits for ready while checking failure and exit witnesses and liveness.
In plain words: I started a job and it never becomes ready; the tool keeps waiting then says target not ready and names the last probe problem such as helper not ready or an unresponsive target.
Start failure path writes a receipt, archives receipts, stops owned processes and scopes, removes the job directory, clears the current job, and re-raises the original error.

remove_job unmounts only private desktop session mounts below the exact job directory and refuses other mounts or missing unmount tools; with keep-frames it retains only frame and marks images plus a dated marker and deletes everything else.
latest_receipts publishes the receipt archive pointer by linking a temporary symlink to the new archive name and atomically replacing the latest pointer, cleaning the temp link afterwards.
persist_receipts archives a job receipts log by copying it to a new file via temp file plus link, refusing to overwrite an existing archive.
Receipt archives are never replaced: both persist and stop use link without replacement and fail with receipt archive already exists; refusing overwrite on collision.
stop shuts down started jobs, copies receipts, appends a stop receipt, removes the job directory, links the archive, and returns receipts handles with optional kept frames.
stop with keep-frames counts only regular frame and marks PNGs and returns their kept list; without it the job directory is fully removed.
This module provides bounded text-only gate helpers that execute vis, log short JSON evidence, and never persist frames.
ROOT derives from the file location, REPORT defaults under docs, VIS is the binary under test, and BASE is the RAM job root for state and cleanup.
CODES maps exit values 0,2,3,4,5,6,7,8,9 to OK, E_USAGE, E_EXPECT, E_RETRIES, E_RULE, E_BUDGET, E_ABSENT, E_TARGET, E_INTERNAL.
require raises AssertionError with default message gate assertion failed when the value is falsy; it is the single assertion primitive.
compatibility_lock ensures parent dirs exist then writes deps.lock pinning wender-agent and vision-engine commits for reproducible gates.
log appends one line to the report while holding an exclusive flock, so concurrent gate processes do not interleave writes.
execute runs a command with timeout, decodes stdout and stderr, attempts JSON parse, and keeps only selected keys plus marks count and STATE for brief mode.
For vis commands execute enforces single-line canonical sorted-keys JSON stdout where rc, ok, code, and verb all agree with the invocation.
execute requires the return code to equal expected when not None, and vis invocations additionally require messages noncanonical stdout and wrong verb on mismatch.
PIDNS reflects test-mode env, SKIP is 77, and skip_started_jobs exits 77 when in test mode but still in the initial PID namespace.
fixture_chrome creates a temporary gate-side chrome shim, points CHROME_BIN at it, registers directory cleanup, and records a TEST MODE note.
not_in_test_mode records NOT COVERED IN TEST MODE and returns PIDNS, marking systemd scope checks as needing a host run.
ORDINARY_TEXTS lists benign hyphenated and URL-like strings and PLACEHOLDER_TEXTS lists filler placeholders, defining the must-type corpus.
synthetic_keys builds fresh random key-shaped strings with upper, lower, and digit mix, plus lowercase hex variants from helper functions.
Helper entry points vis, state, note, cleanup, and sha wrap execution, read job.json, log notes, stop jobs, and hash files.
In plain words, a bad gate shows its command, measured rc, and short JSON evidence in the report, and a vis output shape mismatch stops the gate immediately.
Shell wrapper that cds to repo root then runs all required gate suites via embedded Python and reports a single verdict.
Entry is sh with optional first arg defaulting to --all, forwarded as mode to the embedded Python driver.
set -eu is active so unset variables and failing shell commands abort before gates run.
Only --all, --unit, --must-fail, --real are accepted; any other mode raises SystemExit with usage string.
Maps 4 unit, 8 must-fail plus writer observations, and 1 real suite to their repo-relative gate files; mode filters by kind.
Outside safe_run each suite runs under systemd-run user scope with MemoryMax=4G and MemorySwapMax=0; inside NEWTON_TEST_PIDNS=1 no wrapper is used.
Each gate subprocess gets timeout 600 and brief=False, so full output is logged rather than truncated evidence.
Return code 77 appends to skipped list, any other nonzero appends to failed list with its code; zero means pass.
Failed suites log Failed gate sets with repr list and exit 1 via SystemExit(1).
Any skipped required set logs Skipped gate sets then INCOMPLETE with count and exits 3, so skipped never counts as green.
Tester sees INCOMPLETE with number of skipped sets and the run certifies nothing for them; rerun missing sets instead of treating it as pass.

event(e) increments global n, writes JSON {'events':n,'pid':...} to out with __import__('os').getpid(), and sets label text to 'Events N'.
Both <KeyPress> and <ButtonPress> are bound via bind_all to the same event handler, so keyboard and mouse inputs must share one monotonic counter.
Startup must write {'events':0,'pid':...} to out, schedule focus_force and freeze polling after 100 ms, then enter mainloop; without a writable out path no observation is possible.

No custom error string is defined; the designed failure is a hang: if <out>.freeze exists, freeze() touches <out>.frozen then blocks forever in while True: time.sleep(.1), halting Tk dispatch without signalling any process.
In testers words: I clicked and typed in the window but the counter file still shows 0 and the label still says No events, so inputs are not reaching the handler.
freeze() is re-armed every 100 ms with root.after; once the sentinel exists it never returns, so the single Tk event loop stops processing further inputs while the process remains alive.
Intentionally uncooperative client wrapper for tests: it spawns one child and only signals that child, forcing supervisor escalation.
Run as a script with one CLI argument; sys.argv[1] becomes the counter path shared with the child.
Spawns the sibling event_target.py with sys.executable, resolved from its own file location, passing the counter path.
Ignores SIGTERM in itself before spawning, so a terminate request does not stop the wrapper directly.
Never signals or stops an ancestor; all stop, continue, and terminate signals target only its own Popen child.
Polls for a freeze request via a sentinel file named counter plus freeze-session, then acknowledges by creating counter plus frozen.
Freeze path sends SIGSTOP to the child, breaks the poll loop, then blocks in child.wait while the child remains stopped.
Cleanup resumes a live child with SIGCONT then terminate, waits 2s, and on subprocess.TimeoutExpired escalates to kill and wait.
In testers words: after the freeze is triggered the UI stops counting clicks and keys but stays up, with wrapper and child still alive until cleaned up.

Setup scans high display numbers for a free server identity, starts an isolated display server and fixture with private HOME plus config plus cache plus data plus runtime plus tmp dirs, waits for the counter file, then adopts the display with the server pid.

Helpers read the counter file for events and typed text, parse stored receipts, and wrap act calls for one adopted job, so every check compares before and after counter state with receipt content.
Key shaped text must leave no trace: counter state unchanged after a short wait, and the key absent from both the returned receipt JSON and the stored receipts file.
Ordinary plus placeholder strings must be typed through to the fixture with counter growth and typed suffix match. The gate logs how many were typed as measured evidence.

Stop with kept frames keeps image files plus a kept record, keeps external server and fixture alive, and makes later look see no job with usage error.
Type from file accepts only a job dir file and types its content. A file outside the job and a sensitive user key path are refused with rule error and no input event.

Removed start flag plus ask verb plus ask file check give usage error and create no job dir. Hosted mode act gives rule error with reason naming 'MV_HOSTED=1' and 'core admission' without bypass advice and sends no input.
Tester plain words: after the screen repaints, clicking the old highlighted spot does nothing, the on screen count stays still, and the tool says the region changed since look.
Depends on an external display server binary and a Tk fixture process started as children, plus shared gate helpers for run and assert and corpora.

Map: f1 credential handling, f2 default expectation, f3 adopted exit refusal, f4 auto ids and reuse, f5 mark chaining and staleness, f6 lifecycle wait, f7 reason and action, f9 type file, f10 removed plus hosted, f8 kept frames last.

Harness loads the vis executable as vis_core module via SourceFileLoader and imports shared test helpers from common.
Tests run as Unit unittest TestCase methods; scripted_act and probe_runner are local harnesses for driving do_act.
run_id persists across save_unlocked and a legacy job without it is upgraded once to a stable new id on load.
State receipts record predicate kind, role, name hash and require_stable, keep canonical observation under 1024 bytes, and omit raw names and untrusted fields.
Stop archives each reused run to a distinct path, preserves prior bytes, records run_id on last line, and refuses collision with Failure rc 5.
Latest receipts pointer is a relative symlink swapped atomically on stop, follows the reused job, leaves no dotfiles, and collision keeps prior target.
Failed start receipts still advance the latest symlink per run, and a further persist collision raises Failure without overwriting prior archives.
Act guard allows listed ordinary payload shapes but rejects synthetic secret key payload with Failure rc 5 under hosted-disabled env.
Act attempts are counted per step id with scope per_step_id; same step retries to 4 with 3 attempts while renamed step starts at 1.
Scope collection treats missing procs data as empty and refuses mismatched group or unverified live members with Failure rc 5.

scripted_act synthesizes real PNG frames, mocks load, save, target, rpc, describe, responsive, lifecycle, actor, capture and clock, then asserts exactly one new receipt with schema and verdict mapping.
Desktop act without witness dispatches xdotool key space, reports loop_witness all false, and returns 0 on change versus 3 on no change across ownerships.
Responsive check for desktop issues exactly one host probe with timeout at most 2 for every ownership.
In plain words: if you press a key but the screen looks exactly the same, the act is refused with code 3 instead of passing.

Helper exit_act builds a scripted expect-exit fixture: temp cgroup with optional oom counters, job with client pid 4242, run stub that writes target.exit.json on xdotool key, then delegates to scripted_act with expect exit.

Entry test_f3_expect_exit exercises expect-exit through exit_act: clean client exit passes, failed client or any Xvfb exit fails, oom forces rc 6, missing witness waits then rc 3, web or adopted ownership is refused.
Contract: responsive must never fall back when Tk witness probe times out. For started, adopted and attached, probe Failure 6 with reason probe timed out must surface as Failure rc 8.
Contract: target must check recorded pid start identity for started, adopted and attached before any command. Stale start raises Failure rc 8 and the mocked run is never called.
Contract: omitted expect-change defaults to any. Changed trail passes with expected any, unchanged trail fails rc 3, while explicit none and rectangle 1,0,1,1 are preserved as given.
Invariant: --step is optional and auto ids are unique and reserved even on refusal. Fresh acts get auto-1, auto-2, reusing auto-1 is refused rc 2, and receipts in one dir never repeat a step id.

State machine for marks: passing act sets marks_valid true and marks_sha to frame_sha_after, clicking mark 1 passes only when pre-input frame matches, stale surface refuses rc 2, no-change act clears marks_valid.

Concurrency: do_act must wait for lifecycle lock before budget and rule. Held lock delays at least 0.35s then reaches rule with Failure 5 lock acquired, ACT_LOCK_WAIT is 10, and short wait raises rc 6 with lifecycle in reason.

Failure path: main receipts carry rc, action and redacted reason with len under 200. Cases use reasons target exited, expected visible change not verified, refused, and boom, with actions xy:5,6, typed text, key sha256, and look.

Contract: death_witness prefers app.log over Xvfb noise. It reports app.log: APP_SAID_GOODBYE, orders app.log before xvfb.log, keeps XVFB_REAL_ERROR but drops pci id for fd lines, and oom maps to rc 6 with reason scope memory budget exceeded.
Concurrency: one actor lock per display for every ownership. Started, attached and adopted on :77 exclude each other with rc 5, :78 remains usable, and only two lock files exist outside job dirs.

Test map: sweep collects only dead targets and old kept frames. Deadtarget is stopped and removed, kept-old at 25h is removed, kept-new and live are skipped, actor lock files are never unlinked, and no signal or command is sent.

Contract: jobs are bound to the pid namespace that made them. Loading foreign or legacy pidns raises Failure rc 5 with PID namespace in reason, and sweep skips foreign, legacy and mismatched kept dirs without signal, command or removal.

Config: test pidns mode requires private namespace plus NEWTON_TEST_PIDNS 1, and inherited_memory_cap demands a capped memory.max equal to 8589934592, otherwise raises Failure rc 5 for max or missing files.
In plain words, if the app never writes its exit proof the action just waits about five seconds and then fails with no change instead of passing, which looks like a hang followed by rc 3.

Test-mode start must be refused before any job directory exists when the caller is uncapped: inherited_memory_cap raising Failure rc 5 with reason 'uncapped' prevents engines from running and BASE/job is never created.

stop --keep-frames keeps only frame_1.png, frame_2.png, marks_1.png plus kept.json, drops receipts/job.json/lock/sock and cache, appends stop receipt with kept_frames 3, and calls shutdown only when ownership is started.
type-file input is sandboxed to the job RAM dir: ok.txt with utf-8, sub/deep.txt, and exactly 64KiB max.txt pass rule and preserve full content in args.type under MV_HOSTED 0.

Outside files, symlinks and symlink traversals, fifo, directory, oversize file, missing file and parent traversal are all refused with Failure rc 5, verified with os.open and builtins.open patched to assert 'opened' is never called.
Non-utf8 latin1.txt and a file containing a synthetic key are refused with Failure rc 5 even though they are inside the job dir and within size limits.

On a desktop act interrupted after input check with Failure 'stop after input check', args.type still holds the full file text while action_of returns only 'type-file:ok.txt', so receipts name the file never its content.
Passing and failing type-file acts both record action 'type-file:ok.txt' with rc 0 then rc 3, proving file content never leaks into receipts across settle outcomes.

Dead surfaces are gone at parser level: start with --untrusted and any ask variant fail parse with rc 2, vis start/ask with those flags return rc 2 without creating BASE/job, and 'ask' is absent from parser choices.

run_gates stub harness maps exit codes: --all is 0 when green, 3 when must_fail exit set returns 77, 1 when must_fail skips plus unit fails; --unit ignores must_fail failure; --must-fail propagates rc 3.
With MV_HOSTED 1, act --key space is refused rc 5 with reason containing 'MV_HOSTED=1' and 'core admission' and not containing 'unset'.

Settle waits for the requested rectangle: outside-then-both needs at least 5 samples to pass rc 0; outside-only exhausts ~0.8s budget with rc 3; stale outside regions do not count and a current rectangle change needs at least 6 samples for rc 0.

Positive expectations need both engine regions and verification: any or rectangle with no regions fails rc 3, and with regions but verified False also fails; none passes rc 0 on identical pixels or masked change with empty changed_regions, but fails rc 3 on unmasked transient, final, or unverified.

remove_job only unmounts private fuse mounts under the job root in reverse order with -u -z, leaves sibling and escaped mounts alone and removes the job dir; any unknown mount refuses rc 5 with no unmount command and keeps the directory.
Usage entry vis with empty, wrong, bare look, escaping job, or missing job act all return rc 2; rect accepts '1,2,3,4' but raises Failure on negative, zero size, short, or nonsense values.

Secret detection contract: 14 synthetic keys are all secret, 27 ordinary texts are all non-secret, keys from index 10 onward and placeholders keep their split, redact yields '[redacted]', and lowercase-only shapes plus short prefixes are not secret.
All ordinary texts pass rule and reach xdotool type with --clearmodifiers; every synthetic key is refused by rule with rc 5 under MV_HOSTED 0.

In plain words: if you try to type something that looks like a secret key, nothing is sent to the desktop, the act ends refused with rc 5 before any capture, and the key never appears in the saved receipt.
PID identity uses start time: current pid with fresh identity is alive, same record with start set to 'stale' is not alive, and terminate on an already-dead record sends no signal.

This file is a must-fail gate suite: every refusal must leave the live target event counter unchanged, not merely return a nonzero CLI status. The helper snapshots the counter before and after each call.
Execution enters at main with a started-jobs guard and exits through the module main guard; cleanup stops jobs in reverse order and removes the temporary work directory even on failure.
check_noeffect defines the no-effect contract: read counter bytes, run the call, wait briefly, require identical bytes afterwards, then emit a PASS note and return the call value.
Two concurrent look readers run under an exclusive job lock; both must exit zero with ok true, preserving frame evidence while the actor refusal below stays a negative control.

Concurrent reader responses must match canonical encoding and carry verb look with code OK, plus existing frame and marks files; failures use messages 'concurrent reader refused', 'reader protocol mismatch', 'reader status mismatch', 'concurrent reader evidence was lost'.

Frames must stay in RAM: a disk-backed directory must fail tmpfs validation and a disk-backed job path must be rejected, leaving the disk directory unchanged; failures use 'disk filesystem passed tmpfs guard' and 'disk path accepted'.

Two private jobs must write a marker inside the private home and produce private config files, then stop; host-owned config metadata before versus after is diffed and gated by private_ok with message 'gedit-owned host paths changed; private-session gate did not pass'.

Synthetic key-shaped payloads and secret file reads must be refused with no counter change, while each ordinary corpus string with rc 0 must increment the events field, proving ordinary text reaches input.

Web password typing with ordinary text must be refused rc 5 with unchanged frame hash; button focus succeeds then three no-op clicks return rc 3 and a fourth returns rc 4, each with unchanged pixels; generic guard message is 'gate assertion failed'.
Default hosted mode input must be refused, and a pinned compatibility job must report engine reference starting 7648b258 and also refuse hosted actuation with no counter change.
One display-wide actor lock serializes started, adopted and attached jobs, and holding the job lock forces contended acts to rc 6 with bounded wait, both verified as no-effect on the counter.
Termination must use recorded pid plus start identity; a live bystander spawned by the test with a stale start token must not be signalled and must remain alive, else 'stale identity was signalled'.

Started jobs must show no scope with test-pidns launch and integer memory cap, or show MemoryMax 4294967296 with MemorySwapMax 0; a sparse file over 2 GiB outside excluded caches must force rc 6 with no input.

Removed --untrusted, ask verb, --ask-file, plus E_USAGE rc 2, E_ABSENT rc 7 for unknown node, E_INTERNAL rc 9 via broken job json, and E_TARGET rc 8 via frozen event loop must all leave counter unchanged; frozen target requires message 'target did not block its event loop'.

In plain tester terms, a healthy refusal looks like nothing moved on screen and the background event tally stayed flat; a sick one would show the same calm screen yet the tally crept up, meaning input leaked through.
Final gate requires public rc values 0,2,3,4,5,6,7,8,9 observed with note 'Must-fail: every Strategy section 5 rule represented' and requires private_ok, then stops jobs and removes work.
This gate forces supervisor teardown when the client ignores termination and its child is stopped, then proves no owned live or zombie process, display endpoint, or job directory remains.
Execution enters at main, guarded for direct run, skips jobs started elsewhere, then creates a unique job name and isolated temp workspace for the run.
Test requires subreaper capability before starting; failure raises exact message 'subreaper unavailable' and the teardown scenario does not run.
Start launches the bundled uncooperative client with a counter file, then reads recorded PIDs from persisted job state and the app child PID from the counter for later identity checks.
stat returns a triple of process state, start time, and parent ID parsed from kernel status, or None on missing or malformed data without raising.
tree snapshots live processes, keeps only recorded PIDs whose start time still matches, then transitively adds descendants by parent linkage and returns a PID to start-time map.
Defined supervisor order for this fixture is escalate past ignored termination, wait for the stopped child, then exit; stop is invoked with no preset expected rc.
Test triggers the session freeze marker then polls up to five seconds for the owned child to enter stopped state T or t before attempting stop.
If the child never stops, require fails with exact payload starting 'owned Popen child did not stop' plus current status, proving the precondition was not met.
Stop must report rc 0 and survivors computed by re-reading live identities with matching start times must be empty; otherwise require fails showing result and survivors.
After successful stop the job directory must be gone; otherwise require fails with exact string 'job dir survived'.
If the display endpoint still exists with identical device and inode identity, require fails with exact string 'owned display survived', proving reuse not cleanup.
Finally block reaps only already-reparented zombies with nonblocking wait until no child or timeout, then retries stop only if the job directory still exists; nothing else is signalled.
In plain words: a broken run leaves a stopped child hanging, stop returns nonzero, or the job folder lingers, instead of the clean pass with zero survivors.
Success is recorded as a MEASURED note counting reaped owned PIDs including the termination-ignoring client and stopped child, asserting no live, zombie, display, or directory remains.
This file verifies sparse-file disk accounting for job budgets: cache paths are excluded while evidence and other data remain capped.
The sole test entry is Budget.test_p4_cache_exclusion_keeps_frame_budget, run under unittest with unittest.main guard.
Test loads the vis core under test dynamically from ROOT vis module via SourceFileLoader, not by importing vis directly.
Test isolates filesystem effects with TemporaryDirectory and patches core.jobpath to return that temp root.
A minimal job dict with job equal to budget is passed to core.budget together with files created under the patched job root.
Large files under home/.cache/download and cache/download must not raise; core.budget is called and expected to succeed.
Large files under frames, home/documents, and data/cache must raise; cache exclusion does not extend to data/cache.

This file implements private receipt-bearing visual orchestration using only standard-library process, file and socket primitives, with a stable numeric return-code table mapped to short names.
Credential-shaped text is detected by one anchored pattern plus a body check; is_secret returns True only for a PEM header or a branch whose named body passes _key_body, otherwise False.

A key body needs at least 8 distinct characters; generic keys with dash or underscore need upper, lower and digit, without them letters plus digit; Slack-style bodies need a digit; other provider bodies pass this stage.

Subprocess helper fails with missing executable plus name, command time budget exceeded, subprocess output budget exceeded, and command failed plus trailing stderr; deadline handling also raises operation time budget exceeded.
Subprocess output is bounded during collection: stdout is capped near 8 MiB and stderr near 64 KiB; exceeding either aborts the command rather than growing memory.

Frame storage must be on a memory filesystem; the RAM root is created with restrictive mode, symlink entries are refused, and ownership must match the caller, with exact errors frames require tmpfs, symlink in RAM root and RAM root owned by another uid.

Job names must match a short alphanumeric start plus dot, underscore or dash; unknown names fail with invalid job and symlinked job directories fail with symlink job refused before any state is touched.
Job state is mutated under an exclusive file lock; save writes canonical JSON to a process-specific temporary file then atomically replaces the live state file.

Loading verifies job identity, same process-namespace membership and budget; it upgrades a live state missing run_id under lock; exact errors include unknown job, job identity mismatch and job belongs to another PID namespace text.

Process identity uses caller-owned process status and start time; zombies and non-numeric entries are ignored; record stores pid plus start, alive requires exact start match, present allows dead but still owned entries.
Descendant discovery walks the whole process table and transitively follows parent links from one root; terminate sends TERM only to a currently alive record and suppresses lookup races.
Job RAM use is measured by walking the job directory without following symlinks and skipping two private cache trees; exceeding 2 GiB fails with job RAM budget exceeded.

Engine references start from built-in defaults and can be overridden by an optional dependency lock object with strict shape, size and duplicate checks; exact errors include symlink dependency lock refused, dependency lock too large and invalid dependency lock.
In plain words: capture setup can refuse with frames need memory storage, a bad job name says invalid job, and an oversized job says RAM budget exceeded even when individual files look small.

select_refs plus engines pin reproducible engine sources: defaults are loaded, optionally overridden by dependency-lock commit pins with per-ref selection reasons, then materialized into a cache for later use.
engines with optional target_repo is the setup entry in this range: it resolves refs, creates a per-user cache directory, and returns paths for wender and ve plus selection metadata.
engines requires each pin to be a full 40 lowercase hex SHA; otherwise it fails with engine pin is not a full commit SHA.

Engine fetch refuses symlink cache entries with symlink engine cache refused, rejects unsafe tar members with unsafe engine archive, and reports missing commits with engine commit unavailable plus SHA.

engine_env isolates execution by dropping DISPLAY and fixing PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE and PYTHONPATH to the resolved engine; desktop_env adds per-job HOME, config, cache, data, runtime and tmp directories plus locale and portal settings.

lifecycle serializes per-job operations through a job lock file: non-blocking by default with job operation in progress, optionally bounded waiting with deadline, and rejects symlink locks with job lock symlink.

actor allows one actor per display across started, adopted and attached jobs via a stable display-wide hash lock file that is never unlinked; failures are actor lock symlink and another actor holds this display.
rpc talks to helper.sock with a JSON line, 5s timeout for ping else 35s, 8MB reply cap; transport or parse failure raises target helper unavailable and server error replies map to their rc.
oom_count reads memory.events oom_kill when a cgroup is recorded, else 0; oom_killed reports true only when current count exceeds the recorded oom_kill_base, used to fail targets on scope OOM.
target enforces liveness in order: scope OOM, recorded death witness, recorded pids alive, stopped owned descendants, then desktop window search plus owner state or web ping.

target fails with scope memory budget exceeded, recorded target process died, owned target process is stopped, target window absent or unresponsive, window owner stopped or dead, window owner disappeared, and target is stopped.

responsive probes the target loop, not the server or capture supervisor: web uses CDP ping, desktop uses desktop_responsive; a missing optional witness with rc 7 returns False while other target and budget failures propagate.

desktop_responsive probes only visible windows: Tk targets via in-loop send evaluation and WMs advertising _NET_WM_PING via token round-trip; timeouts fail with Tk target event loop did not respond or target did not answer _NET_WM_PING.

capture prunes with reserve 1, checks budget and target, writes frame plus monotonic timestamp PNG, then rechecks budget: web via RPC capture, framebuffer via engine screen reader, desktop via x11grab; framebuffer faults are framebuffer capture absent and framebuffer read failed or surface disappeared.

In plain words: the app window is gone or frozen so look, check or click reports target window absent or unresponsive, recorded target process died, or target helper unavailable instead of returning a new screenshot.

do_act implements the sampled visual-change protocol: after input it captures frames over settle_ms, tracks transient/onset/stable digests, then calls describe() and decides pass/fail from pixel evidence, changed_regions overlap and verified flag before updating step state and receipt.

Parser/parser() is the CLI entry in this slice: verbs doctor/start/look/act/check/stop/sweep/adopt/attach; act takes step plus input source and op/text/expect-change/mask/settle-ms; check takes predicate plus require-stable.

act allows exactly one of click/xy/type/key/ax/type-file with op limited to click/focus/type; check allows exactly one of state/state-absent/window-title/region-changed-since with require-stable default 2.

Frame-scoped marks are invalidated before input and renewed only on pass: marks_valid is set False after the pre-input capture, then set to passed after verdict with marks_sha updated only when passed, so a later click needs a fresh look.

Stale-mark inputs fail rc 2 before actuation: 'look frame unavailable; renew marks' when the last look frame is missing, and 'target mark changed since look; renew marks' when region_hash of before differs from region_hash of looked box.

expect-change exit waits for target.exit.json inside the settle budget and fails with 'scope memory budget exceeded', 'target exited', 'client exited 0 but another owned process exited: ...', or 'expected exit not observed; target still running'; pass records exit returncode 0 with no after frame.

Sampled verdict fails rc 3 with 'expected visible change not verified' when the any/none/region condition plus verified flag is not met; the receipt carries frame_sha_before/after, changed_regions and sampling diagnostics.

serve() runs one accept loop on the helper socket, sets dead on first child exit with a target.exit.json witness, reaps non-child zombies via owned_descendants and waitpid, and answers stop/ping/state/roles/capture/protected/action serially.

Each act updates step state and loop witness: st gains attempts/passed/changed_regions/before/after, loop_witness after comes from responsive() and obtained is before and after, and oldest_retained_step is recomputed from steps whose before file still exists.

Sampling is bounded in time and count: spacing is max(.04,settle_ms/1000/28), the loop stops at the deadline or samples>=30, and each sample records decode and timing plus slow_factor with settle_degraded when slow_factor>2.

The verdict fuses two signals: pixel_evidence gives different/in_region/sha_before/sha_after with masked bytes copied from before, and describe() changed_regions are filtered by actual_change; any needs regions and difference, none needs neither, region needs in_region plus overlap plus verified.

Input execution splits by target_kind: web sends an rpc action with ax/operation/text/xy/key and uses reply verified, while desktop drives xdotool mousemove with sync plus sleeps and down/up or type/key with clearmodifiers.

In plain words: you clicked or typed but the screen looks the same, so the tool reports expected visible change not verified with before/after frame hashes and an empty or mismatched changed-region list.

Inside the supervisor loop, web actions with xy send move, press, and release mouse events and actions with text insert text, both replying verified true. This is the web actuation branch for the range.
Web key-only input has no path and fails with rc 7 and reason 'web key input unavailable'. Exceptions in the request handler return error and rc, defaulting to 8.
Supervisor teardown ignores termination signals, exits the browser pipe, then terminates descendants, sends continue to stopped ones, waits briefly, escalates to kill, and reaps children before exit.

Scope membership checks that the scope name matches the job, that its resolved path is under the system cgroup root with the same name, and that the manager-reported control group matches before reading members.
Scope ownership is enforced: a nonempty different manager path fails with 'scope ownership not verified', and unverified ownership with members fails the same way instead of signalling.
shutdown_started collects started pids plus owned descendants and scope members, saves them as cleanup_pids, asks the helper to stop, then escalates from wait to terminate to kill with bounded waits.
Shutdown is fail-closed: survivors fail with 'owned process did not stop or reap; job retained' and a nonempty scope fails with 'owned scope is not empty; job retained'.
Test mode uses a small reaper that parents the supervisor, prints its pid, waits for it, then reaps orphans until no children remain, standing in for the user manager.

Test PID-namespace mode requires an explicit flag plus a non-initial namespace; test start then requires the caller cgroup to carry a numeric memory cap or fails with 'test-mode start needs a memory-capped caller cgroup (safe_run)'.
Production start requires session runtime prerequisites: an owned absolute runtime directory, a launcher executable, and a reachable user manager; missing items are returned as a list for the caller.

Missing runtime prerequisites raise Failure 7 with reason starting 'session_runtime_absent: ' and carry cause and prerequisite details; start size, timeout, and memory caps fail with 'invalid size', 'timeout out of range', and 'invalid memory cap'.

Start waits for ready versus failure, target-exit, or supervisor death witnesses, verifies the target and responsiveness, then captures one frame and writes a start receipt; launch, scope-exit, and not-ready paths fail with 'supervisor launch failed: ', 'scope or target exited: ', and 'target not ready: '.

Job removal first detaches only private fuse mounts below the exact owned job root and fails closed with 'unexpected job mount; refusing cleanup', 'private FUSE mount requires fusermount for cleanup', and 'private FUSE mount could not be detached'.
Receipt archiving links a complete adjacent temporary into place with no replacement on collision and refreshes a per-job latest pointer through an atomic symlink swap.
Tester plain words: I started a job and it just says the target is not ready, or the supervisor exited right away, so I never get a usable screen to click.

persist_receipts copies the live receipts log to a per-run archive named by job and run id, hard-links it into place, refreshes the adjacent latest link via latest_receipts, and returns the archive path.

stop terminates started scopes, appends one stop receipt without double-persisting, archives receipts with no-overwrite linkage, optionally retains frame and marks images, removes the job directory, and returns archive locations.
_dispatch routes every CLI verb: doctor, start, act, sweep, adopt, attach, look, check and stop, loading the job for frame verbs and delegating to dedicated helpers.
dispatch serializes look, check and stop through a job lifecycle lock without refusing concurrent readers, and stop additionally takes the display-wide actor lock before teardown.

main sets a bounded operation deadline, parses args, dispatches, prints a canonical envelope with ok, rc, code and verb, maps skill drift to rc 3 and unexpected exceptions to rc 9, and backfills one receipt when none was written.
Receipt archiving never overwrites: both persist and stop fail with rc 5 and reason receipt archive already exists; refusing overwrite when the destination link already exists.
doctor fails with rc 7 and reason starting core unavailable: plus canonical result when desktop tooling is missing or the vision describe help probe fails.

sweep separates retained-frame directories with kept marker and no job file from live jobs with job file, honoring a retention interval and pid-namespace match, and reports removed versus skipped names.

adopt proves Xvfb ownership by liveness plus command name and display identity match, else Xvfb owner not proven or PID is not this display Xvfb; attach requires an owner token match, else owner token missing or different.
look captures a frame, describes it, adds web state for web targets, saves it as last with marks validity, writes a pass receipt with frame hash, prunes old frames, and returns the observation.

do_check requires require-stable between 2 and 20, else --require-stable must be between 2 and 20; region hashes reject out-of-surface boxes with region outside surface; unknown or evicted step baselines fail with unknown step or step baseline evicted messages.

State checks are web only with STATE is web only; OCR is not state; window title is desktop only with X window title is desktop only; bad predicates give STATE predicate requires role=name; uncovered roles give role is outside STATE coverage; opaque subtrees block absence proof.

check passes only when every repeated observation satisfies its condition and all snapshots are identical; region checks additionally require masked pixel evidence inside the box intersecting a reported changed region.
As a tester I waited for a label or region change and the check just says predicate failed or observations unstable with no match, even after retrying the look.

Verbs doctor, start, look, act, check, stop, sweep, adopt, attach manage jobs with lifecycle and display actor locks, receipts, PNG frame capture, vision-engine describe, Xvfb plus desktop supervision or CDP web supervision, secret redaction, RAM budgets, stable predicate checks and cleanup. Thin shell wrapper for install gating and delegation: it validates one mode flag, resolves its own directory, then replaces itself with the sibling Python installer and forwards the mode, so install logic lives outside this file.
Single optional entry argument selects preview or apply mode, defaulting to preview when absent; only two literal mode values pass the case guard and any other value is rejected.
Argument-count contract rejects more than one argument with a usage message on stderr and exit status 2 before any approval check or delegation runs.
Unknown mode prints 'usage: install.sh [--dry-run|--apply]' to stderr and exits 2, without resolving directories or launching the Python step.
Apply mode without approval refuses before delegation: it prints 'E_RULE: --apply requires VISION_INSTALL_OK=1 (VIS_INSTALL_OK=1 also accepted)' to stderr and exits 5.
Strict shell mode is on: the script exits on the first failing command and treats expansion of unset variables as an error.
Depends on an isolated Python interpreter plus the sibling installer file found through physical resolution of the wrapper directory; exec replaces the shell process so nothing after it runs.
Tester words: I ran the installer with no arguments and nothing was installed or changed. That matches the default: with no argument the wrapper selects preview mode rather than applying changes.
Renders, syncs and inspects the four vision skill copies using stdlib only, with template hashing, reference-tree rendering, guarded planning, and dry-run, apply and check modes.
main() accepts exactly one argument among --apply, --dry-run and --check, otherwise prints usage to stderr and returns 2.
Module entry maps Refused and OSError to an E_RULE stderr line and exit 5, so guard and filesystem failures share one refusal code.
targets() defines four destinations: two checkout dist copies for claude and codex plus two home skills/vision copies, with home-only extra guard selected by index.
expected() reads the SKILL.md template, hashes it with sha256, renders path and hash placeholders into the template and every regular file under skill/references, and refuses symlink sources.

guard() requires home targets to resolve outside the checkout, rejects any symlink in the destination path or existing tree, rejects non-directory ancestors, and rejects non-file non-directory entries.
plan() deletes orphans and type-mismatched paths deepest-first, creates needed directories shallow-first, and writes a file only when missing or byte-different.

inspect() reports per copy missing, changed and orphan lists, sets drift true when any copy has missing, changed, orphan or error entries, and reports legacy vis siblings plus a legacy_skill_copy_present warning.
main() validates every destination with guard() and builds the full operation list before creating any directory, then prints each DELETE, MKDIR and WRITE operation in order.
Dry-run prints the planned operations and writes nothing; apply executes DELETE by rmdir or unlink, MKDIR by mkdir, and WRITE by write_bytes after the full validation and planning phase.
--apply requires VISION_INSTALL_OK=1 or VIS_INSTALL_OK=1 in the environment, otherwise it raises Refused with '--apply requires VISION_INSTALL_OK=1 (VIS_INSTALL_OK=1 also accepted)'.
Bad argv prints 'usage: skill_copies.py [--apply|--dry-run|--check]' to stderr with return 2; Refused and OSError print 'E_RULE: ' plus the reason to stderr with exit 5.
Refusals use exact strings: 'symlink in skill source: ', 'home target inside checkout: ', 'symlink in target path: ', 'target ancestor is not a directory: ', and 'unsafe target entry: '.
File comparison and sync read and hold whole file bytes with read_bytes and write_bytes, so peak memory grows with the largest skill file and the full rendered set.
In plain words: a check that prints drift true means one skill copy is missing a file, has different bytes, has an extra file, or hit a guard or filesystem error named in that copy.
Implementation imports only hashlib, json, os, pathlib and sys, so rendering, hashing, inspection output and filesystem sync have no third-party dependency in this file.

This file is the binding contract for the vision skill: one executable using only the standard library drives engines by subprocess, prints exactly one canonical JSON result per verb, sends diagnostics to stderr, and must report uncertainty as failure rather than success.
Exit status is contractual: 0 OK, 2 E_USAGE, 3 E_EXPECT, 4 E_RETRIES, 5 E_RULE, 6 E_BUDGET, 7 E_ABSENT, 8 E_TARGET, never 1 on purpose, with unexpected exceptions reported as E_INTERNAL with rc 9.

Each job owns a private directory with restricted mode on a memory filesystem, verified before use, holding a state file with display, recorded process identities with start times, ownership kind, references and step counters, with job names limited to a safe pattern.

Frames, marks and crops live only in the job directory, at most 40 frames are retained, the per-job file budget is 2 GiB with rc 6 beyond, and only text receipts are copied to the persistent receipts location on stop.

Engine selection uses full commit identifiers from a lock file with per-engine fallback and explicit reason when absent, refuses malformed present pins, probes capabilities instead of assuming them, and never runs from or modifies source checkouts.

Doctor inspects required tools, engines, capabilities, memory and data files, reports per-surface gaps, and with its skill flag compares exact rendered contents and file sets across all four installed copies, signalling drift while legacy copies do not change the result code.

Start launches the target on a private display with no fixed number, runs everything in one memory-capped scope, isolates locale and runtime state inside the job, supports desktop, web over a private socket helper, and electron pixels-only modes, and refuses untrusted programs while waiting for a visible window or page load.

Ownership distinguishes started, adopted and attached jobs: adoption requires a live owned display server process for that display and never kills it on stop, while attachment requires a matching owner token and denies input without an explicit allow flag.
Look captures a frame and describes marks with identifier, geometry, kind and text, plus a structured state object for web only, and never returns raw accessibility trees or page source.

Act requires an explicit change expectation, clicks a mark from the latest look at its box centre with fixed delays, captures before and after images with optional masked regions, and supports a web-only structured-node action whose receipt must show verified success.

Act accounting is strict: missing expectation is rc 2 E_USAGE, a fourth attempt on one step gives rc 4 E_RETRIES without touching the target, reuse of a passed step is rc 2, non-web structured action is rc 7 E_ABSENT, and a dead or frozen target gives rc 8 E_TARGET.

Every act verb enforces hosted-environment refusal with rc 5 E_RULE and no input sent, one actor per display with a second actor refused, refusal of credential-like typing and protected nodes, and input only on started or adopted jobs or explicitly allowed attached jobs.

Every verb that touches or reads the target emits one receipt line with schema identifier, job, step, verb, action, target kind, display, ownership, before and after frame digests, expectation, changed regions, verdict, status codes, attempts, engine references and timing, never carrying pixels and hashing long typed text.

Tester plain words: I clicked a button and the picture looked exactly the same, but the step was marked as passed. The contract forbids that: unchanged frames are never a pass unless no change was requested, and screen text alone can never pass a check.
vision lets an agent run a program, see it, act on it, and prove what happened for acceptance that depends on a rendered interface, paired with the agent's own tests rather than replacing them.

The fast path is doctor once, then start a job, look, act on a mark, act with typed input, look again to read back meaning, exit with an expected-exit act, then stop and cite the receipt archive path.
For web, start from a page URL, act with an accessibility-node click operation, then read back with an exact role-equals-name state check, which is web only.

Exit codes are contractual: 0 passed, 2 bad arguments or reused passed step, 3 expected change did not happen, 4 step retry budget used, 5 safety refused, 6 budget, 7 capability missing, 8 target died or froze, 9 internal error.
An act pass proves only its declared visible change. Acceptance needs a read-back before the exit act and stop, either a check pass receipt or an inspected frame cited by its content hash.

rc 3 means the expected change did not happen and rc 8 means the target died or vanished; both are possible real bugs requiring look and diagnose. rc 5 means a safety rule refused and must not be bypassed.
Tester plain words: I clicked the button but the screen looks exactly the same as before. That maps to an rc 3 expectation failure, not a pass, and needs a fresh look and diagnosis.
Run one job per worker, each with its own private display. Acts on one job are serialized and one actor is allowed per display server; a second concurrent actor is refused.

Frames stay in volatile job memory and are never stored on disk. Hosted image use needs operator consent because there is no hosted judge; text-only workers must judge structured state and change regions.

Before launching N jobs, read doctor once for missing desktop, web, electron, and session runtime plus free volatile memory, then admit jobs within the per-job memory budget with margin and size the per-job memory cap from free RAM.
Never drive an inherited or person-owned display. Trusted programs only: the private display isolates only the display, not files or network, so untrusted programs need a capsule.

Do not use vision for headless API, service, CLI, unit-test, or static-check decisions. Godot belongs to another skill, and Windows, macOS, mobile, and Wayland are not possible and must be reported as such.

Reported evidence is version-scoped: an independent false-green set at 17 of 17, zero failures in a 20-cycle stability run under load, and seeded-bug finds in 4 of 4 fresh-agent tasks, with a cold-agent rerun on the newer tree still not done.
